questions.question: Who among the following has written the famous novels (originally in Bangla) ‘Devdas’ and ‘Parineeta’?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay** was a renowned **Indian Bengali novelist** and **short story writer**.
 
• He is best known for his novels **‘Devdas’** and **‘Parineeta’**, which have been adapted into several films in different languages.
 
• His works are celebrated for their **depiction of the social issues** and **human emotions** of the time.
 
• Chattopadhyay's writing style is known for its **simplicity** and **realism**.
 
• He is considered one of the greatest authors in **Bengali literature**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rabindra Nath Tagore**__

 __
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore** was a **polymath**, known for his contributions to **literature, music, art, and philosophy**.
 
• He won the **Nobel Prize in Literature** in 1913 for his collection of poems **‘Gitanjali’**.
 
• Tagore's works include novels, short stories, songs, dance-dramas, and essays.
 
 
 
• **Nabin Chandra Sen**__
 __
 
• **Nabin Chandra Sen** was a **Bengali poet** and **writer** known for his **epic poem** **‘Raivatak’**.
 
• He is also renowned for his patriotic writings and contributions to **Bengali literature**.
 
 
 
• **Bankim Chandra Chatterjee**__
 
 
• **Bankim Chandra Chatterjee** was a significant **Bengali writer** and **poet**, famous for his novel **‘Anandamath’**.
 
• He is also the author of **‘Vande Mataram’**, which later became a **national song of India**.

questions.question: In which of the following states is shifting agriculture locally called Penda?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shifting agriculture**, also known as **slash-and-burn agriculture**, is a farming practice where trees and vegetation are cut down and burned to create fields for cultivation.
 
• In **Andhra Pradesh**, this practice is locally called **Penda**.
 
• This method is commonly used by indigenous and tribal communities in various regions around the world.
 
• **Shifting agriculture** is typically employed in areas with nutrient-poor soils, allowing farmers to use the ash as fertilizer.
 
• After a few years of cultivation, the land is left fallow to recover its fertility, and the community moves to a new area to repeat the process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Orissa**__

 __
 
• In Orissa, shifting agriculture is known as **Podu**.
 
• Podu cultivation is mainly practiced by the tribal communities in the hilly regions of the state.
 
 
 
• **West Bengal**__
 __
 
• In West Bengal, shifting agriculture is referred to as **Jhum** cultivation.
 
• It is commonly practiced by tribal groups in the northeastern parts of the state.
 
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh**__
 
 
• In Madhya Pradesh, shifting agriculture is known as **Bewar** or **Dahiya**.
 
• This practice is mainly observed in the tribal areas of the state.

questions.question: Analgesic medicines are used for _________________.

options.text: correcting deficiencies due to vitamins and nutrients
killing or weakening microbes and infections

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**reducing pain and in fever**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Analgesic medicines** are primarily used to **alleviate pain**.
 
• They work by **blocking pain signals** from reaching the brain or by interfering with the brain’s interpretation of these signals.
 
• Analgesics are commonly used to treat conditions such as **headaches, muscle pain, arthritis, and other chronic pain conditions**.
 
• Examples of analgesic medicines include **paracetamol (acetaminophen), ibuprofen, and aspirin**.
 
• Some analgesics, such as **opioids**, are prescribed for more severe pain and must be used under medical supervision due to their potential for **addiction and side effects**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **supporting physiological functions**__

 __
 
• Medicines that **support physiological functions** are generally known as **supportive or adjunctive therapies**.
 
• They help in maintaining the **normal functioning of the body** or enhancing the effectiveness of other treatments.
 
 
 
• **correcting deficiencies due to vitamins and nutrients**__
 __
 
• Medicines for **correcting deficiencies** include **vitamin supplements and nutritional supplements**.
 
• These are used when there is a lack of essential nutrients in the body, leading to conditions like **scurvy (vitamin C deficiency) or rickets (vitamin D deficiency)**.
 
 
 
• **killing or weakening microbes and infections**__
 
 
• Medicines that **kill or weaken microbes** are known as **antimicrobials**, which include **antibiotics, antivirals, antifungals, and antiparasitics**.
 
• These medicines are used to treat **infections** caused by various pathogens such as **bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites**.

questions.question: Who among the following was the captain of the Indian cricket team during the 1983 Cricket World Cup event?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Kapil Dev**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kapil Dev** was the captain of the **Indian cricket team** during the **1983 Cricket World Cup.**
 
• Under his captaincy, India won its first-ever **Cricket World Cup** on **25th June 1983**.
 
• Kapil Dev is regarded as one of the greatest all-rounders in the history of cricket.
 
• He was awarded the **Wisden Indian Cricketer of the Century** in 2002.
 
• Kapil Dev's leadership and remarkable performance, including the famous **175 not out** against Zimbabwe, were crucial in India's World Cup triumph.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sandeep Patil**__

 __
 
• **Sandeep Patil** was a key player in the Indian cricket team during the 1983 Cricket World Cup.
 
• He is known for his aggressive batting style and played a significant role in the semi-final against England.
 
 
 
• **Sachin Tendulkar**__
 __
 
• **Sachin Tendulkar** made his debut in international cricket in 1989, six years after the 1983 World Cup.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Master Blaster" and holds numerous records in international cricket.
 
 
 
• **Mohinder Amarnath**__
 
 
• **Mohinder Amarnath** was the vice-captain of the Indian team during the 1983 World Cup.
 
• He was named the Man of the Match in both the semi-final and final of the 1983 World Cup.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an important function of the Supreme Court?

options.text: It acts to check on executive authorities and enforce the rule of law
It maintains of land records and revenue collection
It is the protector and guarantor of fundamental rights

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It maintains of land records and revenue collection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court** of India has several important functions, but **maintaining land records and revenue collection** is not one of them.
 
• The responsibility for maintaining land records and revenue collection typically falls under the purview of **state governments** and their respective **revenue departments**.
 
• The primary functions of the Supreme Court include:
 
 
• **Judicial Review**: It acts to check the powers of the executive and legislative branches and ensure laws are consistent with the Constitution.
 
• **Federal Equilibrium**: It ensures the balance of power between the central and state governments.
 
• **Protection of Fundamental Rights**: It acts as the guardian of the fundamental rights of citizens enshrined in the Constitution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **It acts to check on executive authorities and enforce the rule of law**__

 __
 
• The Supreme Court has the power of **Judicial Review**, allowing it to invalidate laws and executive actions that violate the Constitution.
 
• This function ensures the **enforcement of the rule of law** and prevents misuse of power by the executive.
 
 
 
• **It maintains federal equilibrium**__
 __
 
• The Supreme Court has the authority to resolve disputes between **states and the central government**.
 
• This function maintains **federal balance** and prevents conflicts of jurisdiction.
 
 
 
• **It is the protector and guarantor of fundamental rights**__
 
 
• The Supreme Court ensures that the **fundamental rights** of citizens are not violated by the state or any other authority.
 
• It has the power to issue **writs** for the enforcement of these rights.

questions.question: The Ebony, Mahogany, Cinchona etc. are trees found in which type of forests in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical Evergreen Forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tropical Evergreen Forests** are characterized by dense and multi-layered vegetation.
 
• These forests are also known as **rainforests** due to their constant high levels of rainfall.
 
• Trees in these forests, such as **Ebony**, **Mahogany**, and **Cinchona**, are known for their **hardwood** and are highly valuable.
 
• The climate in these forests is typically **hot and humid** throughout the year.
 
• They are mainly found in regions with an annual rainfall of over **200 cm**.
 
• These forests are home to a wide variety of **fauna**, including many **endangered species**.
 
• In India, tropical evergreen forests are primarily located in the **Western Ghats**, **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**, and the **Northeastern states**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tropical Deciduous Forests**__

 __
 
• Also known as **monsoon forests**, these forests shed their leaves during the dry season.
 
• They are found in regions with **moderate rainfall** (70-200 cm annually).
 
• Common tree species include **Teak**, **Sandalwood**, and **Sal**.
 
 
 
• **Thorny Forests**__
 __
 
• These forests are adapted to **arid and semi-arid regions**.
 
• Common vegetation includes **cacti**, **acacias**, and **euphorbias**.
 
• They are mainly found in parts of **Rajasthan**, **Gujarat**, and the **Deccan Plateau**.
 
 
 
• **Mangrove Forests**__
 
 
• Mangrove forests are found in **coastal regions**, particularly in **estuaries and deltas**.
 
• They are adapted to saline and brackish water conditions.
 
• Commonly found along the **Sundarbans** in West Bengal.

questions.question: Who was the first feudatory of Pallavas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijayalaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vijayalaya** was the founder of the **Chola dynasty** in South India.
 
• He captured Thanjavur (Tanjore) and made it his capital around the mid-9th century.
 
• Vijayalaya initially served as a **feudatory of the Pallavas** before establishing his own independent kingdom.
 
• The Chola dynasty under Vijayalaya and his successors expanded and became one of the most powerful and culturally sophisticated empires in South India.
 
• The Chola rule saw significant advancements in **art, architecture, and maritime trade.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Harshvardhan**__

 __
 
• **Harshvardhan** was an Indian emperor who ruled North India from 606 to 647 CE.
 
• He was not related to the Pallavas but was the ruler of the **Vardhana dynasty**.
 
• His capital was **Kannauj**, and he is known for his support of Buddhism and extensive literary contributions.
 
 
 
• **Rajendra**__
 __
 
• **Rajendra Chola I** was a significant ruler of the Chola dynasty who succeeded **Rajaraja Chola I**.
 
• He is known for his extensive military conquests and for expanding the Chola Empire beyond South India.
 
• Rajendra Chola I established a new capital at **Gangaikonda Cholapuram**.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka**__
 
 
• **Ashoka** was an Indian emperor of the **Maurya Dynasty** who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent from 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• He is known for his role in the spread of **Buddhism** across Asia.
 
• Ashoka's reign predated the Pallavas by several centuries.

questions.question: All living organisms on the Earth are made up of carbon compounds. Many years ago, dead and buried plants started slowly modifying into coal under high temperature and high pressure. This process is called:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**carbonization**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbonization** is the process by which **dead and buried plants** slowly transform into **coal**.
 
• This transformation occurs under conditions of **high temperature** and **high pressure**.
 
• The process involves the **chemical decomposition of organic materials** by heating them in the absence of air, leading to the formation of **carbon-rich substances**.
 
• **Coal** is primarily composed of carbon, hydrogen, sulfur, oxygen, and nitrogen.
 
• Coal is used as a **fossil fuel** for generating electricity, steel production, and as a liquid fuel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Black gold formation**__

 __
 
• The term **"black gold"** is often used to refer to **crude oil** due to its high economic value.
 
• It is not related to the formation of coal but is a term used in the context of **petroleum**.
 
 
 
• **Peat formation**__
 __
 
• **Peat** is an accumulation of partially decayed vegetation or organic matter.
 
• It is the first stage in the formation of coal and is found in **wetland areas**.
 
• Peat can be used as a source of **fuel** and for **horticultural purposes**.
 
 
 
• **Composting**__
 
 
• **Composting** is the process of recycling organic waste into **fertilizer**.
 
• It involves the **decomposition** of organic matter by microorganisms in the presence of oxygen.
 
• Compost is used to **enrich soil** and improve plant growth.

questions.question: What kind of structures are generally used by Buddhists for containing remains of their monks and nuns?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stupas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stupas** are significant religious monuments in Buddhism used to house the **relics of monks and nuns**.
 
• A stupa is generally a **hemispherical structure** symbolizing the burial mound of Buddha.
 
• They often contain **relics and sacred texts** related to Buddhism.
 
• Stupas serve as a place of **meditation and veneration** for Buddhists.
 
• Some of the most famous stupas include the **Sanchi Stupa in India** and the **Boudhanath Stupa in Nepal**.
 
• They are not just religious sites but also **architectural marvels** with intricate carvings and detailed designs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Grihas**__

 __
 
• **Grihas** are generally referred to as **houses or residential buildings** in ancient Indian texts.
 
• They are not specifically used for religious purposes or for containing relics.
 
 
 
• **Viharas**__
 __
 
• **Viharas** are Buddhist **monasteries** where monks and nuns reside.
 
• They serve as **centers of learning and meditation** but are not typically used for containing relics.
 
 
 
• **Garbha Griha**__
 
 
• The term **Garbha Griha** refers to the **sanctum sanctorum** or the innermost sanctum of a Hindu temple.
 
• It houses the **main deity** of the temple but is not used in Buddhist traditions for containing relics.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Viceroy of India during the announcement of the Partition of Bengal in 1905?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Curzon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Curzon** was the **Viceroy of India** from 1899 to 1905.
 
• The **Partition of Bengal** was announced in 1905 and was one of his most controversial decisions.
 
• The partition was aimed at **dividing Bengal** into two provinces to improve administrative efficiency.
 
• The partition led to widespread protests and was seen as an attempt to **divide and rule** by creating religious divisions.
 
• The decision was eventually reversed in 1911 due to the strong opposition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lord Hastings**__

 __
 
• **Lord Hastings** served as the **Governor-General of India** from 1813 to 1823.
 
• He is known for his role in the **Third Anglo-Maratha War**, which led to the end of Maratha power in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Dalhousie**__
 __
 
• **Lord Dalhousie** was the **Governor-General of India** from 1848 to 1856.
 
• He is known for the **Doctrine of Lapse** and for introducing the **Railways** and **Telegraph** in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Canning**__
 
 
• **Lord Canning** served as the **Governor-General of India** from 1856 to 1862.
 
• He was the first Viceroy of India and is known for his role during the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**.

questions.question:

 List II (President)

 (b) Rash Behari Ghosh

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bombay, 1885** - **Womesh Chandra Bannerjee** was the president of the first session of the Indian National Congress held in Bombay in 1885.
 
• **Calcutta, 1896** - The session held in Calcutta in 1896 was presided over by **Rahimtullah M. Sayani**.
 
• **Surat, 1907** - The Surat session in 1907 was presided over by **Rash Behari Ghosh**. This session is notable for the split between the Extremists and the Moderates in the Congress.
 
• **Kanpur, 1925** - **Sarojini Naidu** was the president of the Kanpur session in 1925. She was the first Indian woman to preside over a session of the Indian National Congress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rahimtullah M. Sayani**__

 __
 
• He was a prominent Congress leader and presided over the 1896 session in Calcutta.
 
• He emphasized the need for unity and self-reliance among Indians during his presidential address.
 
 
 
• **Rash Behari Ghosh**__
 __
 
• He was a noted legal luminary and presided over the 1907 Surat session.
 
• This session is historically significant due to the split between the Extremists and the Moderates.
 
 
 
• **Sarojini Naidu**__
 __
 
• She was a prominent poet, freedom fighter, and the first Indian woman to become the president of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Her presidency in the 1925 Kanpur session marked a significant moment in the history of the Congress.
 
 
 
• **Womesh Chandra Bannerjee**__
 
 
• He was the first president of the Indian National Congress.
 
• His leadership in the 1885 Bombay session set the foundation for the Congress as a pivotal organization in the Indian freedom struggle.

questions.question: Jaiminiya and Kausitaki dances are mentioned in which of the following?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Brahmanas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Brahmanas** are a collection of ancient Indian texts with commentaries on the **Vedas**.
 
• They provide explanations of the hymns in the Vedas and guide the performance of Vedic rituals.
 
• The **Jaiminiya** and **Kausitaki** are two of the various **Brahmanas** that exist.
 
• The Jaiminiya Brahmana is associated with the **Sama Veda**, while the Kausitaki Brahmana is linked to the **Rig Veda**.
 
• These texts are crucial for understanding the development of Indian religious and philosophical thought.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Agamas**__

 __
 
• **Agamas** are a collection of scriptures that provide detailed instructions on temple construction, worship rituals, and the philosophical doctrines of Hinduism.
 
• They are widely used in **Shaivism, Vaishnavism, and Shaktism** traditions.
 
 
 
• **Puranas**__
 __
 
• The **Puranas** are ancient Hindu texts that narrate the history of the universe from creation to destruction and the genealogies of gods, heroes, and sages.
 
• They are classified into **Mahapuranas** and **Upapuranas**.
 
• Examples include the **Bhagavata Purana** and the **Vishnu Purana**.
 
 
 
• **Vedas**__
 
 
• The **Vedas** are the oldest and most authoritative scriptures of Hinduism.
 
• They consist of four main collections: **Rig Veda, Sama Veda, Yajur Veda, and Atharva Veda**.
 
• Each Veda has four parts: **Samhitas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, and Upanishads**.

questions.question:
Match the columns.

 
 

 List-I (South Indian King)
 List-II (Dynasty)
 
 

 1. Maravarman Sundara Pandyan
 A) Hoysalas
 
 

 2. Krishnadevaraya
 B) Chalukyas
 
 

 3. Narasimha II
 C) Pandyas
 
 

 4. Tailapa III
 D) Tuluvas
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maravarman Sundara Pandyan** belonged to the **Pandya dynasty**.
 
• **Krishnadevaraya** was a ruler of the **Tuluva dynasty**, which was part of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• **Narasimha II** was a ruler from the **Hoysala dynasty**.
 
• **Tailapa III** was a king from the **Chalukya dynasty**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hoysalas**__

 __
 
• The **Hoysala dynasty** was prominent in South India between the 10th and 14th centuries.
 
• They are well-known for their **architectural contributions** such as the temples in **Belur, Halebidu, and Somanathapura**.
 
 
 
• **Chalukyas**__
 __
 
• The **Chalukya dynasty** ruled large parts of southern and central India between the 6th and 12th centuries.
 
• They are known for their contributions to **art and architecture**, notably the **temples at Badami, Aihole, and Pattadakal**.
 
 
 
• **Pandyas**__
 __
 
• The **Pandya dynasty** was one of the ancient Tamil dynasties, ruling regions of South India for several centuries.
 
• They are famous for their **trade and commerce** with Roman and Greek merchants.
 
• They also made significant **contributions to Tamil literature and culture**.
 
 
 
• **Tuluvas**__
 
 
• The **Tuluva dynasty** was the third ruling dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• The most famous ruler of this dynasty was **Krishnadevaraya**, who is known for his military conquests and patronage of art and literature.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered as a day of mourning among the Muslim community?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Muharram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muharram** is the first month of the Islamic calendar.
 
• It is one of the four **sacred months** of the year in which warfare is forbidden.
 
• The event of **Yawm Ashura** (the 10th day of Muharram) is particularly significant for Shia Muslims.
 
• On this day, Shia Muslims commemorate the **martyrdom of Imam Hussein**, the grandson of Prophet Muhammad, in the Battle of Karbala in 680 AD.
 
• For Sunni Muslims, it is a day of fasting to honor the day that Moses and the Israelites were saved from Pharaoh.
 
• **Public processions** and reenactments of the Battle of Karbala are common among Shia communities during this month.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Bakri Eid**__

 __
 
• **Bakri Eid**, also known as **Eid al-Adha**, is celebrated to honor the willingness of Ibrahim (Abraham) to sacrifice his son as an act of obedience to God.
 
• It involves the **sacrifice of an animal** such as a sheep, goat, cow, or camel, and the meat is distributed among family, friends, and the needy.
 
 
 
• **Shab-e-Barat**__
 __
 
• **Shab-e-Barat** is observed as the night of forgiveness or atonement.
 
• It is believed to be the night when God decides the fortunes of people for the coming year and forgives the sins of those who repent.
 
• Muslims often spend the night in prayer and may visit graves of loved ones to offer prayers for their souls.
 
 
 
• **Barah Wafat**__
 
 
• **Barah Wafat** marks the death anniversary of Prophet Muhammad.
 
• It is observed on the 12th day of the Islamic month of Rabi' al-awwal.
 
• Muslims commemorate the event with prayers, recitations of the Prophet's teachings, and acts of charity.

questions.question: As per Planning Commission of India, in 2004–05, the percentage of total population of India below poverty line (Lakadawala Poverty Estimates combined) was:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**27.5%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Planning Commission of India**, the percentage of the total population of India below the poverty line in **2004–05** was **27.5%**.
 
• The estimation was based on the **Lakadawala Poverty Estimates combined**.
 
• The poverty line is measured based on the **minimum income required to meet basic needs** such as food, shelter, and clothing.
 
• The poverty estimation methodology has been developed over time to better capture the socio-economic conditions of the population.
 
• In 2004-05, the criteria for measuring poverty were primarily based on **consumption expenditure**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lakadawala Poverty Estimates**__

 
 
• The **Lakadawala Committee** was formed in 1993 to review the methodology for poverty estimation.
 
• It recommended that poverty lines should be updated using the **Consumer Price Index**.
 
• The committee's estimates were based on **calorie intake norms**, ensuring a certain level of calorie intake per person per day.
 
• These estimates were widely used for planning and policy-making until the introduction of the **Tendulkar Committee Report** in 2009.

questions.question: Who first postulated that cells are generated from pre-existing cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudolf Virchow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rudolf Virchow** was a renowned German physician, anthropologist, pathologist, prehistorian, biologist, writer, editor, and politician.
 
• He is credited with the famous statement "**Omnis cellula e cellula**" which means "all cells come from cells".
 
• This theory was a significant contribution to the **cell theory** and changed the understanding of cell reproduction and growth.
 
• **Virchow** is often referred to as the "**Father of Modern Pathology**" due to his significant contributions to the field.
 
• He emphasized that diseases are caused by malfunctioning cells, which shifted the focus of medical research to cellular pathology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jennifer Doudna**__

 __
 
• **Jennifer Doudna** is an American biochemist known for her pioneering work in **CRISPR gene editing**.
 
• She was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Chemistry** in 2020, along with Emmanuelle Charpentier, for the development of a method for **genome editing**.
 
 
 
• **William Harvey**__
 __
 
• **William Harvey** was an English physician who made groundbreaking contributions to the understanding of **blood circulation**.
 
• He is best known for his work on the **systemic circulation** and properties of blood being pumped to the brain and body by the heart.
 
 
 
• **Carl Linnaeus**__
 
 
• **Carl Linnaeus** was a Swedish botanist, zoologist, and physician who laid the foundations for the modern biological naming scheme of **binomial nomenclature**.
 
• He is often referred to as the "**Father of Modern Taxonomy**".

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India lays down qualifications for the membership of the Parliament?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 84**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 84** of the **Constitution of India** specifies the qualifications required for membership of **Parliament**.
 
• According to this Article, a person must be a **citizen of India** to be eligible for election as a member of Parliament.
 
• The person must not be less than **25 years of age** for the House of the People (Lok Sabha) and **30 years of age** for the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
 
• He/she must possess such other qualifications as may be prescribed by or under any law made by **Parliament**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 105**__

 __
 
• **Article 105** deals with the **powers, privileges, and immunities of Parliament** and its members.
 
• This Article grants freedom of speech in Parliament and immunity from legal action for anything said or any vote cast in Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Article 85**__
 __
 
• **Article 85** pertains to the **sessions of Parliament**, **prorogation** and **dissolution**.
 
• It mandates that the President shall summon each House of Parliament at such intervals that there should not be more than **six months gap between the last sitting** in one session and the date appointed for its sitting in the next session.
 
 
 
• **Article 80**__
 
 
• **Article 80** deals with the **composition of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha)**.
 
• It specifies the number of members, their election/nomination, and the representation of States and Union territories.

questions.question: It is observed that a child's heart rate is 135 times per minute. The beat frequency of heart is ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.25 Hz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **heart rate** refers to the number of times the heart beats per minute.
 
• The **beat frequency** of the heart is the number of beats per second.
 
• To convert the heart rate from beats per minute to beats per second, we divide by **60**.
 
• In this scenario, the child's heart rate is **135 times per minute**.
 
• Dividing 135 by 60 gives us the beat frequency: **135/60 = 2.25 Hz**.
 
• Therefore, the beat frequency of the heart is **2.25 Hz**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **8100 Hz**__

 __
 
• This value is **incorrect** as it does not correspond to the heart rate conversion process.
 
• Such a high frequency is more typical of **sound waves** or other high-frequency phenomena.
 
 
 
• **1.12 Hz**__
 __
 
• This value is **incorrect** because it is not the result of dividing 135 by 60.
 
• A beat frequency of 1.12 Hz would correspond to a heart rate of **67.2 beats per minute**, which is much lower than 135 beats per minute.
 
 
 
• **135 Hz**__
 
 
• This value is **incorrect** because it mistakenly assumes that the heart rate in beats per minute is the same as the beat frequency in Hz.
 
• 135 Hz would imply an extremely high heart rate of **8100 beats per minute**, which is not physiologically possible.

questions.question: Recreation services are an example of ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**consumer goods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Recreation services** fall under the category of **consumer goods** as they are directly used by individuals for personal satisfaction and enjoyment.
 
• **Consumer goods** are products that are purchased for consumption by the average consumer.
 
• These goods can be categorized into **durable goods** (such as cars and furniture) and **non-durable goods** (such as food and clothing).
 
• Recreation services, such as amusement parks, theatres, and sports events, provide entertainment and leisure activities to consumers, fulfilling their **recreational needs**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **capital goods**__

 __
 
• **Capital goods** are goods used in the production of other goods or services. These include machinery, buildings, and equipment.
 
• They are not directly consumed by consumers but are used to create products that are then sold to consumers.
 
 
 
• **intermediate goods**__
 __
 
• **Intermediate goods** are products that are used in the production process to produce other goods. They are not final goods and are typically used to produce consumer or capital goods.
 
• Examples include raw materials like steel, wood, and components like microchips.
 
 
 
• **inferior goods**__
 
 
• **Inferior goods** are goods for which demand decreases as the income of consumers increases. These goods are typically lower-cost alternatives to more expensive goods.
 
• Examples include generic brands and off-brand grocery items.
